questions.q: Which treatment plan applies to me?
questions.a: Fluorouracil and folinic acid on Days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 and 36; oxaliplatin also on Days 1, 15 and 29. Two weeks off follow. Three 56-day cycles make a planned 24-week course. Your team confirms any modification.

questions.q: Do more side effects mean treatment is working?
questions.a: No. Side effects do not reliably measure response. Report symptoms and follow the agreed review plan.
Ask the team to replace example numbers with working daytime, out-of-hours and backup contact routes before leaving.

title: FLOX: fluorouracil, folinic acid and oxaliplatin
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending
context_label: Adjuvant stage II or III colon cancer after resection
indication_text: Adjuvant stage II or III colon cancer after complete resection.
purpose: FLOX is given after surgery for selected stage II or III colon cancer to reduce the chance of recurrence. It combines weekly fluorouracil/folinic acid with oxaliplatin on alternate treatment weeks.
schedule_summary: Fluorouracil and folinic acid on Days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 and 36; oxaliplatin also on Days 1, 15 and 29. Two weeks off follow. Three 56-day cycles make a planned 24-week course.
administration_text: Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² IV over 2 hours on Days 1/15/29 before folinic acid 500 mg/m² over 2 hours; fluorouracil 500 mg/m² bolus 1 hour after folinic acid starts. Folinic acid/5-FU also Days 8/22/36. Oxaliplatin in glucose 5%, never saline. Three 8-week cycles.

agents.name: Oxaliplatin
agents.explanation: Oxaliplatin makes links within DNA. These interfere with copying and repair, which can stop a cancer cell dividing. Healthy tissues can also be affected.
agents.watch: Cold can trigger tingling or throat discomfort. Tell the team about persistent numbness, difficulty with buttons or walking, or infusion symptoms. New breathing difficulty always needs assessment.
risks: Persistent sensory neuropathy, sometimes lasting after treatment
Rare serious lung or blood complications

agents.name: Folinic acid
agents.explanation: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself.
agents.watch: The combined treatment can increase mouth soreness and diarrhoea. Report these promptly. Rare allergic reactions can occur.

agents.name: Fluorouracil
agents.explanation: Fluorouracil interferes with DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The same drug has different schedules; follow the prescription for this regimen.
agents.watch: Report diarrhoea, mouth sores, painful hands or feet and unexpected severe early symptoms. Chest pain needs urgent assessment even after a normal DPD test.
risks: Severe early toxicity including DPD-related toxicity

phases.label: Prescribed treatment course
phases.short: Adjuvant stage II or III colon cancer after resection
phases.detail: Fluorouracil and folinic acid on Days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 and 36; oxaliplatin also on Days 1, 15 and 29. Two weeks off follow. Three 56-day cycles make a planned 24-week course.

day_groups.title: Six weekly treatment visits
day_groups.body: Attend on Days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 and 36; oxaliplatin only on Days 1, 15 and 29. Side effects can occur on any day; the calendar does not predict when you will feel well.
day_groups.action: Call the oncology team if unwell. Report symptoms before the next dose; do not wait for your next appointment if urgent.

day_groups.title: Planned two-week break
day_groups.body: No catch-up doses; symptoms can continue during the break. Confirm the next plan. Side effects can occur on any day; the calendar does not predict when you will feel well.
day_groups.action: Call the oncology team if unwell. Report symptoms before the next dose; do not wait for your next appointment if urgent.

chronology_notes.title: Symptoms can continue
chronology_notes.text: Contact oncology for fever, sudden illness, diarrhoea, mouth soreness or inability to drink, during treatment or the break.

support.title: Supportive medicines
support.text: Use the prescribed anti-sickness and diarrhoea plan; check the medicine, timing and rescue duration. Do not duplicate steroids or anti-sickness medicines.

support.title: Mouth, bowel and skin care
support.text: Report soreness and diarrhoea early. Use gentle mouth and skin care and ask for help with food or fluids.

support.title: Medicine checks
support.text: Bring all prescription medicines, supplements and non-prescription products. Warfarin and phenytoin may need closer monitoring; brivudine/sorivudine interactions require pharmacy review.

support.title: Cold precautions
support.text: Avoid cold exposure as advised after oxaliplatin. Do not suck ice chips during this regimen.

sections.title: Before treatment
sections.text: Confirm the treatment aim, duration, DPD result, blood tests, prescription and contact numbers.

sections.title: Visits and access
sections.text: Fluorouracil and folinic acid on Days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 and 36; oxaliplatin also on Days 1, 15 and 29. Two weeks off follow. Three 56-day cycles make a planned 24-week course.This regimen does not require a home infusion pump.

sections.title: If treatment is delayed
sections.text: Ask for revised written treatment and support-medicine instructions. Do not make up missed doses or carry an old plan into a new phase.

sections.title: Getting help
sections.text: Keep the wallet card and medicine list available. Contact the team promptly for infection, dehydration, chest symptoms or significant toxicity.

urgent_extra: Contact oncology immediately for fever, shivering, sudden illness, severe diarrhoea, inability to drink, very little urine or unusual bleeding. New severe chest pain, collapse or major breathing difficulty needs emergency help.
consent_support: Confirm treatment aim, expected benefit, reasonable alternatives and no-treatment/supportive-care options. Discuss DPD, infection, mouth/bowel/skin toxicity, cardiac symptoms, fertility, contraception, breastfeeding and interactions. Discuss persistent neuropathy and infusion reactions.

items.title: Why this treatment?
items.text: FLOX is given after surgery for selected stage II or III colon cancer to reduce the chance of recurrence. It combines weekly fluorouracil/folinic acid with oxaliplatin on alternate treatment weeks.

items.title: Your course
items.text: Fluorouracil and folinic acid on Days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 and 36; oxaliplatin also on Days 1, 15 and 29. Two weeks off follow. Three 56-day cycles make a planned 24-week course.

items.title: Choices
items.text: Discuss the expected benefit, burdens, alternatives and how treatment fits your priorities. You can ask for more time or another explanation before deciding.

items.title: DPD before fluorouracil
items.text: Low DPD activity can cause severe toxicity. Testing helps guide the plan but cannot prevent every reaction. Unexpected severe early symptoms need urgent advice.

items.title: Blood tests
items.text: Before each weekly treatment: blood count, renal and liver profile; baseline DPD. Scans/markers follow the consultant plan.

items.title: Chest / heart

items.title: Bowel / hydration

items.title: Throat / breathing
items.text: Report throat tightness or breathing difficulty promptly; the team must assess the cause.

items.title: Food and fluids
items.text: Aim for tolerable meals and fluids. Report weight loss or poor intake; ask for dietetic support.

items.title: Activity and rest
items.text: Adjust activity and rest to your energy. Report fatigue that limits normal tasks.

items.title: Fertility and sexual health
items.text: Ask about fertility preservation before treatment and the contraception and breastfeeding plan for all medicines. Report a possible pregnancy promptly.

items.title: Support for you and your family
items.text: Ask about counselling, psycho-oncology, practical support, transport and financial advice. Bring someone to discussions if helpful.

evidence.title: Understanding the evidence
evidence.intro: Ask which evidence matches your treatment aim.
evidence.interpretation: NSABP C-07 tested adding oxaliplatin to weekly bolus fluorouracil/leucovorin after stage II/III colon cancer surgery. FLOX is not the 46-hour-pump FOLFOX regimen. Group results do not predict your individual benefit.
